testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When backing up, should you use a helper?

options.text: No, a helper often causes confusion.
Only if you don't feel confident.
No, they would get in the way.

questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper whenever you can. They can watch your blind spots and keep you safe.

questions.question: Which tire condition is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of 2/32 inch

questions.explanation: Check your tires for: front tire tread depth of at least 4/32 inch, rear tire tread depth of at least 2/32 inch, no cracks, proper air pressure, and equal sizes. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat or drink.
With one hand at a time, switching hands.
With a cracked grip for better control.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel. This gives you proper control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a rear-end crash. It also makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and wave with the other hand.
Do not use the brakes at first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes at first.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, braking can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes unless you must stop to avoid a crash. Let your vehicle slow down first. Then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: What is required to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
Provide your job history from the last five years.
Provide a list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check during a pre-trip tire inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your tires for: front tire tread depth of at least 4/32 inch, rear tire tread depth of at least 2/32 inch, no cracks, proper air pressure, and equal sizes. Different manufacturers are acceptable.

questions.question: What do drivers often do when stuck behind a slow vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If you are being tailgated, let the other driver pass.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Say nothing and hope it goes away.
Write a report about the problem.
Avoid using that part and hope no one notices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report about the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, you may need to write a report about the vehicle. Report any problems that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brakes. An air brake system uses compressed air to operate.

questions.question: Why do dry bulk tanks need special care?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and loads shift during travel. Be extra careful when turning or going around curves with these vehicles.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on gear use. Which should you avoid?

options.text: Select a gear that does not rev the engine.
Forget to shift through an intersection.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on gear use. Pick the right gear for engine speed, avoid grinding gears, and do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how much does your braking distance increase?
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase stopping power needed and braking distance. When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance multiplies by four.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, what should you do to ensure normal stopping power?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Set the control to the neutral position.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Always set it to "normal" to get full stopping power. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power. Front wheel braking works well in all conditions.

questions.question: What is the general length limit for a 2-vehicle combination with load?
questions.explanation: Under Wisconsin law, a 2-vehicle combination including the load cannot be longer than 65 feet.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, safely pull over and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What is the purpose of headers?

options.text: Protect the driver during a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver during a crash
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: What should you do if mirrors are dirty before starting a trip?

options.text: They will likely become clean after driving a short distance.
It should not be a concern.
They should be cleaned before the vehicle is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be cleaned before the vehicle is driven.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check, clean the mirrors and windshield if they are dirty. You need a clear view to drive safely.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives, such as ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: How should you inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, place wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check it does not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air brakes start working:

options.text: Only when it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air brakes cannot work instantly. Air takes time to travel through the lines to reach the brakes. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between pushing the pedal and when the brakes actually begin to work.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Create more space between you and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create more space between you and the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: When someone is tailgating you, increase the space in front of your vehicle. This makes it easier for the other driver to pass you. Speeding up will not help, because the other driver may continue tailgating at the higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice any safety problems or possible mechanical issues, you should:

options.text: Wait to see if the problem goes away.
Write about the problems in your report.
Try to fix the issue yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write about the problems in your report.
questions.explanation: At the end of your driving shift, you may need to write a report about your vehicle's condition. Always mention anything that could affect safety or cause mechanical problems.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes:

options.text: You do not need to worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, check your mirrors and blind spots, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A one-way check valve:

options.text: Drains water and oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks.
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Keeps the spring brakes in place until they are needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the main air tank. It prevents air from escaping the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure signs include a loud bang from a blowout or heavy thumping and vibration in your vehicle. If steering feels heavy or the rear fishtails, stop and check your tires. Smoother steering is not a sign of tire failure.

questions.question: Carrying too much cargo in your vehicle:

options.text: Usually has no effect on the vehicle.
Can make steering and braking harder to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make steering and braking harder to control.
questions.explanation: Overloading your vehicle can hurt steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to recognize when cargo is too heavy or not balanced properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Driving distractions fall into three types: physical (reaching for something), mental (talking with passengers), or both (using a hand-held phone). Obtuse is not a type of distraction.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Fatigue warning signs include difficulty focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, heavy head, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable. Staying in your lane is not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, you should shift into a lower gear:

options.text: After you have already started going downhill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before you start going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster on the downhill slope, so you need to be prepared.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what should you expect?

options.text: It will stay green as you approach.
It will change from green directly to red, skipping yellow.

questions.explanation: When a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will likely turn yellow soon. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do first when alley docking?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: First, drive past the alley and stop parallel to its edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley space.

questions.question: If a load is found to be too long during a pre-trip inspection, what should the driver do?

options.text: Reduce the length of the load.
Make sure all required flags and lights for the oversize load are secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all required flags and lights for the oversize load are secure.
questions.explanation: If the load is oversize, check that all warning signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly mounted and secure. Make sure you have all required permits.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you don't know which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, leave the vehicle and wait for firefighters.

questions.question: What type of vehicle must you use for the on-road driving skills test?

options.text: You can use any vehicle for the test.
You must use the same type of vehicle for which you want to be licensed.
The vehicle type does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the same type of vehicle for which you want to be licensed.
questions.explanation: Your on-road driving test must be taken in the same type of vehicle for which you want to get your license.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, what should you verify?

options.text: The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses are empty of fluid.

questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pump, and fluid level. Look for and fix any leaks before driving.

questions.question: What is one way to avoid driving aggressively?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead with realistic travel times to avoid frustration. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include: driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, avoiding gestures at other drivers, and keeping both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat and you hear a loud bang, when will the truck be affected?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is at the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay between when the tire fails and when you feel it affect the truck. This delay might make you think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a hill, what is your best option to stop?

options.text: Let the vehicle drift to a stop.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill grade, use an escape ramp to stop safely.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS is not working, how should you brake?

options.text: Press the brake pedal as hard as possible.

questions.explanation: Without a working ABS system, your regular brakes still function. Drive and brake normally, and have your ABS repaired soon.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Wet roads have less traction. Reduce your speed by about one-third when driving on wet roads.

questions.question: How does poor weight balance affect your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle harder to control and unsafe to drive.

questions.question: When drivers turn, where do they usually look?

options.text: In the direction of the turn
In the opposite direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: Drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. Even without a signal, a driver's body movements can show they plan to turn.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle parked, what should you do?

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is out of gear

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. If needed, chock the wheels.

questions.question: Why should you accelerate slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because you should always accelerate slowly
So you do not lose control of your vehicle
So you do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead
To be the last vehicle through an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: So you do not lose control of your vehicle
questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on roads with poor traction can cause you to lose control. Always accelerate slowly and smoothly in these conditions.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have a low center of gravity
They usually have a high center of gravity
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have a high center of gravity
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. Drive carefully with them because the contents can shift during travel.

questions.question: What is the purpose of multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions give you extra gears. They are controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.

questions.question: How often should you stop to rest while driving?
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles. This helps prevent fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you don't know how to put it out, what should you do?

options.text: Try to douse the flames with water
Move away from the flames and wait for firefighters

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the flames and wait for firefighters
questions.explanation: If you are unsure how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away from the flames and let firefighters handle it. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: Why should you check your tires regularly in hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure may increase with temperature
Tread wears down faster in hot weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with temperature
questions.explanation: Hot weather increases air pressure in tires. Check your tire pressure and mounting carefully when driving in heat.
